Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Sr. Advocate, assisted by Mr. Ganesh
Kandpal and Mr. Alok Mehra, Advocates for the petitioners.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel, and Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief
Holder, for the State/respondents.
August 18, 2015

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 In all these above titled petitions, identical
controversy is involved, hence are being adjudicated
together by this single judgment.
 All the petitioners were initially appointed as
Assistant Teachers in the Junior Basic Schools in District
Bageshwar. Most of them were posted in Block Garur or
Kapkot of such district. Needless to add that the post of
Assistant Teacher (Basic) is a block level cadre post. At
some point of time, it was realised by the District
Education Officer (Basic) that none of the teachers is
inclined to perform the services in the remote areas of such
blocks. So, an advertisement was published on 13.8.2011
at his initiation alluring those teachers for early/out of turn
promotion who accept to render their services in remotest
places. All these petitioners responded and they were given
out of turn promotion and were sent to the schools in the
remote places. Thus, they have become either the
Headmaster of the Junior Basic Schools or the Assistant
Teacher in the Senior Basic Schools, the names whereof
were divulged in the advertisement itself. The benefit of the
offer was conferred only seniority-wise to the teachers, who
offered their services in consonance of the advertisement.
The above step of the District Education Officer
(Basic) annoyed a number of teachers, who though seniors

6
in the list but then had been at quite a junior position as
against the petitioners and their resentment was led by one
Mr. Sushil Joshi by way of filing the writ petition in the
Court. The coordinate Bench of this Court disposed of the
petition, inter alia, on 15.12.2014 asking the writ
petitioners to present themselves before the District
Education Officer (Basic), Bageshwar on 22.12.2014 and
such officer was also directed to remain present in his
office to hear the grievances.
 The officer heard the grievances of those
petitioners and cancelled the promotion order of all these
petitioners and ordered recovery of the pay and other
allowances which they received as against the promotional
post. Feeling aggrieved with the orders of the officer
concerned, they all have approached this Court.
 The Court has rendered hearing to learned Sr.
Counsel as well as other concerned Counsels nay the
learned Standing Counsel on behalf of the State.
 Undisputedly, the promotional exercise of the
Basic Teachers can be initiated under the Uttar Pradesh
Basic Education (Teachers) Services Rules, 1981 and the
seniority of such teachers is to be determined in
accordance with the Seniority Rules of 2002. The
promotional rules formulated in the undivided State had
been adopted by this State too under the Reorganisation
Act. Thus, the promotional exercise can be initiated subject
to the Rules of 1981, as adopted by this State, and the
seniority of the teachers is to be determined and settled
strictly in accordance with the Rules of 2002, and no other
method can be introduced by any authority howsoever high
he may be dehoring such rules.
 It is quite explicable that issuing an
advertisement dated 13.8.2011 was quite contrary to the
rules applicable for the promotions. It was the brainchild of

7
the authority concerned himself, which he could not and
must not have done. So, the cancellation of all these
promotions is quite valid. But at the same time, the factor
cannot be ignored that all these petitioners resumed their
duties in remote areas as a result of their promotion by the
authority concerned and, all the more, rendered their
services for 3-4 years in the area. So, the salary and other
allowances received by them for the promotional posts
cannot be recovered from them.
 In the helm of controversy, as has been
discussed above, the District Education Officer (Basic) is
directed to make the seniority list afresh strictly in
accordance with the Rules of 2002 and then he is at liberty
to initiate the proceedings of promotion as well as transfer
in order to ensure that the imparting of education may not
suffer in the remote areas of the District Bageshwar. He will
take such exercise as early as possibly, but within four
weeks by all means. Hitherto, any other list vis-‡-vis to the
seniority of such teachers prepared at the whims of such
officer is hereby quashed.
 It is hereby also made clear that District
Education Officer (Basic) will take care of the postings of all
the teachers in the remote areas of the hills of District
Bageshwar at the earliest and as per the Transfer Rules
2013 and whosoever teacher defies such order, stern
disciplinary action must be taken against him inasmuch as
to place him under suspension and to the extent of
dismissal from the service.
 With the directions as above, all these petitions
stand disposed of.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
Prabodh/Nadim
